title: When the Mountains Bloom
summary: Five days on the rhododendron trails of Northwest Yunnan

searchKeywords: Lijiang → Maxiang Road → Luoguqing → Shaxi → Lijiang or Dali

paragraphs:
This is not a summit trek or a race against the clock. It is a carefully paced journey for travellers who want to walk through Yunnan’s quieter mountain country while remaining connected to the people and places that shape it.
The main hike in Luoguqing can be adapted to the group, from a gentler woodland walk to a fuller day among grasslands, streams and rhododendron slopes. Before and after the trail, Lijiang and Shaxi bring the journey back to the old Tea Horse Road — through stone lanes, caravan history and evenings that invite you to slow down.

seasonNote.title: A Note about the Flowering Season
seasonNote.body: May to July is the broad flowering season, but the exact timing varies with elevation, weather and conditions in each particular year. We cannot guarantee that any specific date will coincide with peak bloom. Our Yunnan-based team will follow recent flowering reports and adjust the walking route where conditions allow.

items.title: Walk through Yunnan’s wild rhododendron season
items.description: Follow a mountain road where rhododendrons bloom across entire hillsides, their colours changing with altitude, weather and light.

items.title: Choose a trail that feels right for you
items.description: Luoguqing offers more than one way into the landscape. Your local guide will shape the walking day around your experience, energy and current trail conditions.

items.title: Enter the landscapes of the Pumi people
items.description: The forests and grasslands around Luoguqing are also lived-in landscapes, shaped by generations of Pumi families, grazing animals and seasonal mountain life.

items.title: Let the journey slow down in Shaxi
items.description: After the mountains, spend a night in Shaxi, where the old theatre, stone lanes and Yujin Bridge still carry the quieter rhythm of the Tea Horse Road.

items.title: Travel privately and leave room for the unexpected
items.description: A private journey keeps the pace flexible, with room to respond to the day and no compulsory shopping stops.

days.title: A quiet beginning
days.logistics: Arrive in Lijiang · Overnight in Lijiang
paragraphs:
Arrive in Lijiang, where our local team will meet you at the airport or railway station and take you to your hotel.
The first day is intentionally light. Rest after your journey, or take an evening walk through Lijiang or quieter Shuhe, allowing your body to settle before heading into the mountains.

days.title: Into the flowering highlands
days.logistics: Lijiang → Maxiang Road → Luoguqing · Overnight in Luoguqing or Tongdian
paragraphs:
Leave Lijiang behind and travel into the lesser-visited mountains west of Jianchuan. As the road climbs, farmland gives way to open slopes, wind-shaped ridges and wild rhododendrons.
We pause where the flowers and conditions are at their best, with time for unhurried walks and photography rather than a hurried roadside stop. Later, continue towards Luoguqing and settle into a simple locally run guesthouse near the mountains.

days.title: Forests, grasslands and rhododendron trails
days.logistics: Hiking in Luoguqing · Overnight in Luoguqing or Tongdian
paragraphs:
Today is the heart of the journey. Walk with a local mountain guide through mossy forest, clear streams, open grasslands and slopes coloured by seasonal rhododendrons.
The route is adapted to the group and current trail conditions. It is designed as an easy-to-moderate mountain walk rather than a technical trek, with time to pause, photograph and experience the landscape without rushing.

days.title: From mountain country to the Tea Horse Road
days.logistics: Luoguqing → Shaxi · Approx. 3 hours / 110 km · Overnight in Shaxi
paragraphs:
Leave the highlands and travel approximately three hours to Shaxi. Along the way, mountain country gradually gives way to cultivated valleys and village landscapes.
Arrive with time to settle into your guesthouse before exploring Sideng Square, the old theatre and the lanes surrounding the former caravan market. Towards evening, walk to Yujin Bridge as the last light settles over the valley. Staying overnight allows you to experience Shaxi after the day visitors have left.

days.title: One last slow morning
paragraphs:
Begin with a quiet morning in Shaxi: tea, breakfast and a final walk through the old town before the streets fully wake.
Later, travel onwards to Lijiang or Dali for your next hotel, railway journey or flight. If you have more time, this journey can also be extended into a longer exploration of Dali, Lijiang or the walking routes of Northwest Yunnan.
